_comment: CANONICAL heartbeat-ack wire fixture. Committed in BOTH vizora-tv and Vizora and
asserted against in both, because the ack crosses a process boundary that nothing
else checks. Keep the two copies byte-identical.
READ THIS BEFORE EDITING — the file is split in two on purpose.
serverAck.*      what the server ACTUALLY EMITS today. Expected OUTPUT of
DeviceGateway.handleHeartbeat(). Asserted in Vizora at
realtime/src/gateways/heartbeat-ack-contract.spec.ts, which drives
the real handler and compares its return value against these.
clientAccepted.* the SUPERSET the client must tolerate — every field vizora-tv acts
on, including ones the current server never sends. This is CLIENT
COMPATIBILITY COVERAGE, NOT a server promise. Asserted in vizora-tv
at src/vizora-app.spec.ts.
The previous version of this file had only the second kind and labelled it the server
contract. That was wrong in a way worth recording: it described
commands:[{type:'reload'}] and revoked:true as the heartbeat response, when the server
emits commands:[] always and has never emitted revoked at all. A server-side test bound
to that shape could only have been made to pass by NOT looking at the server. A fixture
must be expected output, never input that manufactures the output.
That is this subsystem's whole history. reconcileContent was wired on both sides, green
on both sides, and ALWAYS undefined at runtime until the .data unwrap landed.
contentVersion went unwhitelisted and every heartbeat was rejected for four releases.
content:impression.timestamp was typed string while both clients send a number, and that
table held zero rows for the repo's lifetime. Every one passed its own side's tests.
If you change this file the corresponding test fails in BOTH repos — that is the point.
Change it only when the wire format genuinely changes, and change both sides.
Vizora realtime/src/gateways/device.gateway.ts handleHeartbeat has exactly four return
statements. The two SUCCESS shapes are below; the two error shapes (createErrorResponse,
rate-limited and caught-exception) carry no data payload and are not part of this contract.
The envelope wrapper { success, data, timestamp } comes from createSuccessResponse
(realtime/src/gateways/dto/index.ts). The client hand-unwraps `.data` (vizora-tv
src/main.ts:1017). Neither side imports the other.
device.gateway.ts:1902-1906 — the normal path, reached when the heartbeat arrives on
the device's CURRENT socket. reconcileContent is computed per-device by
shouldReconcileContent(); `true` here is one legal value and the contract test drives
the real handler for both true and false.
commands is a HARDCODED EMPTY LITERAL at this site. The key is part of the wire shape;
it has never carried data. Commands are delivered by the separate `command` socket
event (device.gateway.ts:2314 live, :2142 offline replay).
device.gateway.ts:1804-1807 — returned when the beat arrives on a socket that is no
longer the device's active one. NOTE THE DIFFERENCE: no reconcileContent key. A
contract test asserting one fixed key set for all success paths would be wrong about
this one, and would break the first time a stale socket beat.
NOT A SERVER PROMISE. The union of everything vizora-tv's ack handler acts on
(src/main.ts:1017-1030), used to prove the client stays correct if any of it ever
arrives. Field by field, against the CURRENT server:
reconcileContent  genuinely emitted today (see serverAck.activeSocket)
commands          key emitted today but ALWAYS []. A non-empty array has never been
reachable in a heartbeat ack. Kept here because the revocation
contract (vizora-tv docs/design/revocation-contract.md §7.1a(a))
names the ack's commands array as an authenticated channel for
`unpair`, so the client must handle it.
revoked           NEVER emitted by the current server. Permitted-but-optional by
design: revocation-contract.md §3.2 says the ack MAY carry it and
§6.3 calls the ack flag optional. Delivered today by the separate
`device:revoked` event. The client branch must stay.
nextHeartbeatIn   emitted by the server, but the client does not read it — it
hardcodes its own 15s interval (main.ts:954-961).
Both shapes below carry the same fields: the client accepts the wrapped envelope OR a
bare unwrapped payload, and must behave identically for either.
